name: Lattice relation detection (LLL/BKZ), low-density subset-sum attacks, and hidden-subset-sum algorithms
description: Equal-sum disjoint pairs of subsets are exactly vectors z in {-1,0,1}^n in the relation lattice L(a) = {z in Z^n : sum z_i a_i = 0} (rank n-1, determinant about ||a||_2/gcd). LLL (Lenstra-Lenstra-Lovasz 1982) and BKZ (Schnorr-Euchner 1994) find short vectors; Lagarias-Odlyzko (1985) and Coster-Joux-LaMacchia-Odlyzko-Schnorr-Stern (CJLOSS 1992) showed that low-density subset-sum instances (density below about 0.6463 and 0.9408 respectively, given an SVP oracle) are solved by reducing the lattice spanned by the a_i and target. If the support lies in a rank-d GAP the relation lattice contains an (n-d)-dimensional sublattice of very short vectors, so reduction reveals the GAP rank as a gap in successive minima. Luo-Li-Li (arXiv 2412.04967) is a different problem: deterministic recovery of a hidden multiset from all its k-subset sums, not relation-lattice detection.
authors_year_venue: [uncertain] A. K. Lenstra, H. W. Lenstra, L. Lovasz, Math. Ann. 261 (1982); J. C. Lagarias and A. M. Odlyzko, J. ACM 32 (1985) 229-246; M. J. Coster, A. Joux, B. A. LaMacchia, A. M. Odlyzko, C. P. Schnorr, J. Stern, Computational Complexity 2 (1992) 111-128; C. P. Schnorr and M. Euchner, Math. Programming 66 (1994); P. Nguyen and J. Stern, CRYPTO'99 (hidden subset sum, orthogonal lattice); J.-S. Coron and A. Gini, CRYPTO 2020 (poly-time HSSP); L. Luo, C. Li, Q. Li, 'Deterministic algorithms to solve the (n,k)-complete hidden subset sum problem', arXiv:2412.04967v2 (24 Feb 2025), math.CO.
status_and_verification: [uncertain] LLL/BKZ/LO/CJLOSS: classical peer-reviewed, recalled, not re-read; density thresholds 0.6463 and 0.9408 are from memory. arXiv 2412.04967: read in full via alphaXiv (abstract, definitions, Algorithms 1-2, Theorems 1-6, conclusion); preprint, no refereed venue seen. The Nguyen-Stern and Coron-Gini items are known only from the reference list and comparison table of 2412.04967.
key_theorem_or_bound: [uncertain] Luo-Li-Li Thm 1: brute-force deterministic algorithm for (n,k)-complete HSSP over R in time O( C(n,k) ( log C(n,k) + prod_{i=1}^{k-1} (C(n-k+i, i) - i) ) ). Thm 2: if sum_{i=1}^u (-1)^{i-1} (i-1)! S(u,i) C(n-i,k-i) != 0 for u=1..n (equivalently the Moser polynomial sum_{j=1}^k (-1)^{j-1} j^{u-1} C(n,k-j) != 0), a symmetric-polynomial/Vieta algorithm recovers the multiset in time O( sum_{u<=n} p(u,<=k)^3 + C(n,k) n ). Recalled (unverified): LO85 solves instances of density d < 0.6463 with an SVP oracle; CJLOSS improves to d < 0.9408; LLL gives approximation factor 2^{(n-1)/2} in poly time.
regime_exponents: [uncertain] Low-density attacks need density n/log2(max a) below about 0.94, i.e. magnitudes above 2^{1.06 n}: exactly the regime where solutions are unique and the relation lattice has no short ternary vectors beyond the planted one. For magnitudes 2^{cn} with c < 1 there are about 2^{(1-c)n} equal-sum pairs and the relation lattice has many short vectors (Gaussian heuristic lambda_1 about sqrt(n/(2 pi e)) * det^{1/(n-1)} which is O(sqrt n) for c = O(1)). The paper 2412.04967 has no exponent window (it is exponential in n for k about n/2). 0.311n, 0.5n, 0.661n not addressed.
proof_type_and_tools: Lattice: LLL/BKZ basis reduction, Gaussian heuristic, Minkowski, orthogonal lattice (Nguyen-Stern). For 2412.04967: algebraic/combinatorial (symmetric polynomials, power sums, Newton identities, Vieta, Stirling numbers; Lemma 1 explicit inverse of A_{k+1}).
quantitative_loss: [uncertain] LLL approximation factor 2^{O(n)} in the worst case (about 1.02^n in practice, heuristic); BKZ-beta reaches root-Hermite factor about beta^{1/(2 beta)}, with time 2^{O(beta)}. To find a ternary relation of support Theta(n) one needs approximate-SVP within a constant factor sqrt(n) of lambda_1, which at n<=40 is easily solved exactly but asymptotically takes exponential time, so no polynomial detection of Theta(n)-length relations.
worst_case_vs_average_case: [uncertain] LLL is worst-case polynomial but with weak guarantees; success of LO/CJLOSS attacks is average-case/heuristic (random a_i with the planted solution being the unique shortest vector); for structured or adversarial a_i the guarantees fail, though GAP-structure detection via successive minima is robust for rank-d GAPs with small box.
coefficient_set: Relations naturally in {-1,0,1} (two disjoint subsets with equal sum); the subset-sum target version uses {0,1} with a target. The hidden multiset problem uses 0/1 incidence matrices with exactly k ones per row.
subset_size_regime: [uncertain] Lattice vectors of Euclidean norm sqrt(k) are relations with total support |P u Q| about k; hence Theta(n)-support relations correspond to norm sqrt(Theta(n)), which is the Gaussian-heuristic scale, so these are among the shortest vectors but cannot be isolated from other short non-ternary vectors without a ternary-structure filter. 2412.04967 is for fixed k-subsets (all k-subset sums), k <= n/2.
relevance_to_Nc: [uncertain] N_c counts ternary short vectors of L(a) with balanced signs and Theta(n) support. Lattice reduction gives a way to enumerate them for n<=40 (enumeration/ sieving in dimension about 40) and an estimate of N_c by counting lattice points in a ball (Gaussian heuristic gives about 3^n-type volume / det).
relevance_to_Dstar: [uncertain] Low-rank GAP structure of the support S (rank d) implies d-dimensional quotient: L(a restricted to S) has an (|S|-d)-dimensional short sublattice, hence k-dissociation fails at small k, matching the repo's lemma (k-dissociated gives D* >= C(m/4+j,j)^2). Reducing the lattice of the support and reading off the shortest ternary relation length k_min gives a computable certificate for D* <= bound or for the absence of short relations (large D*).
applicability_gap: (i) LLL guarantees are exponentially weak for the Theta(n)-norm regime; (ii) low-density theory assumes a planted unique solution, not a counting statement about many pairs; (iii) {-1,0,1} constraints are not captured by a Euclidean ball (need to filter ternary vectors); (iv) polynomial doubling not used; (v) 2412.04967 targets recovery from complete k-subset sum data, not relation detection, so it does not give a lattice tool, and its algorithms are exponential (C(n,k)).
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Random a_i of size 2^{cn} with c above about 1.06 (low-density, safe from LO/CJLOSS); rank-d GAP supports with random generators (relation lattice has short rank n-d part); Sidon/dissociated sets (no short ternary vectors); instances with density near 1 where lattice attacks fail.
dependency_chain: [uncertain] Final detection step after structure results: large bin or small D* (inverse_littlewood_offord, fourier_large_spectrum_bohr) implies low-rank GAP implies reduction of the relation lattice reveals it (this item), then constructive APs (dissociated_sidon_structure) or dynamic programming over the GAP solve the instance. In the other direction, dissociation tests use the same lattice.
constructiveness: LLL is polynomial-time and constructive; BKZ with block size beta has 2^{O(beta)} cost; exact SVP in dimension about 40 takes seconds to minutes. 2412.04967 algorithms are deterministic but exponential: O(sum p(u,<=k)^3 + C(n,k) n) for the Vieta method (uniqueness required, fails when a Moser polynomial vanishes) and a product-of-binomials brute force.
lean_formalizable: [uncertain] LLL termination and the size-reduction lemmas could be formalized but are long; the correspondence 'ternary vector in L(a) iff equal-sum disjoint pair' is trivial. Not a priority for the repo's mathlib-free setting.
computational_check: [uncertain] No experiments in 2412.04967 (theory/complexity tables only). In the repo, n<=40 relation-lattice reduction with fpylll/own LLL plus enumeration is well within reach; scripts/analysis could compute the shortest ternary balanced relation length k_min and compare to the k(delta) thresholds (k=0.105n at delta=0.311).
next_experiment: [uncertain] For each repo family at n=24, 32, 40 build the relation lattice of the support S (|S|=n/2), run LLL then BKZ-20, record successive minima lambda_i and k_min (shortest ternary balanced relation), and test the prediction that rank-d GAP supports show a gap between lambda_{|S|-d} and lambda_{|S|-d+1} while dissociated supports have none.
open_issues: No known polynomial algorithm detects Theta(n)-length ternary relations; low-density density thresholds recalled from memory; the item description's pairing of 2412.04967 with relation-lattice detection is a mismatch (it concerns the (n,k)-complete hidden subset sum problem and its multiple-solution (singular pair) theory, and Algorithm 2 fails exactly when a Moser polynomial vanishes).
